notes.1a: (b) All four parts were answered very well with most candidates gaining full credit.
notes.1c: Many correct answers using the equation speed = distance / time and showing full working were seen . In almost every case, incorrect answers had no working, so no credit could be given.
notes.2ai: Few correct answers were seen. Candidates did not seem to recognise that the Sun is the source of wind energy.
notes.2aii: There appeared to be confusion between the workings of a generator and a turbine, with turbine being a common incorrect answer.
notes.2b: A significant number of candidates gave advantages that were too vague, e.g. “a clean source of energy”, “environmentally friendly”, “less contamination”. More detailed specific answers were required.
notes.3ai: Full working is required for a ‘show that’ question and many candidates achieved full credit. Other candidates just gained partial credit for the equation. There were a significant number of candidates who did not give any answer. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2023 (ii) Most of the candidates who answered (i) correctly also gave the correct answer here. Other candidates needed more practice with cross multiplication. Again, several candidates did not offer an answer.
notes.3b: The majority of candidates attempted this question with many getting the correct answer. A common error was to multiply the weight by 9.8 instead of dividing by 9.8.
notes.4ai: Very few candidates realised that the liquid would expand when the temperature increased.
notes.4aii: Most candidates gave the correct answer.
notes.4b: Most candidates realised that the pressure would decrease. Fewer stated that this was because the particles were moving more slowly. Only a few linked the decrease in speed to less frequent collisions with the wall or collisions with less force.
notes.4c: Many correct answers were seen here, generally with full working shown. Other answers usually gained partial credit for recall of the pressure equation which was subsequently rearranged incorrectly.
notes.5a: The majority of candidates gave the correct answer but there was often a lack of working here.
notes.5bi: (ii) The majority of candidates gave the correct answers to these questions.
notes.5biii: Very few candidates recognised that the frequency was equal to the number of waves (peaks) passing the pointer divided by the time taken to pass the pointer.
notes.5c: Candidates who were able to recall the wave equation generally achieved full credit. A significant number of candidates did not give an answer.
notes.6ai: A large number of correct answers were seen but a common error was γ -ray (i.e. the symbol γ not the word gamma). A noticeable number of candidates did not give an answer.
notes.6aii: Many candidates lacked the knowledge for this question. In addition, again a number of candidates did not give a response.
notes.6bi: Most candidates knew another use for X-rays, but some answers were too vague, e.g. “to see through things”, “security”. More detailed answers were required.
notes.6bii: Few candidates displayed sufficient knowledge about the required precautions. Most answers were at the level of “wear special glasses”, “protect their eyes”, “use special protection” and “have enough protection”.
notes.7a: (b) The majority of candidates lacked the knowledge for these questions. A number of candidates did not give a response.
notes.8a: The majority of candidates gave the correct answers.
notes.8bi: Many correct answers were seen here, generally with full working shown. Other answers usually gained credit for recall of the V = I R equation which was subsequently rearranged incorrectly. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0625 Physics June 2023 (ii) Candidates who were able to recall the equation P = I V and the unit generally achieved full credit. A number of other candidates gained partial credit for recalling the unit. A number of candidates did not give a response.
notes.9ai: A large number of correct answers were seen. A common error was interchanging the locations of the electrons and neutrons.
notes.9aii: Candidates generally lacked knowledge of term ‘isotope’. Some confusion between an ion and an isotope was seen.
notes.9b: A significant number of candidates gave sources that were too vague to credit, e.g. “industry”, “reactions”, “factories”, “hospitals” and often “radon gas”, which was given in the question.
notes.9ci: (ii) Many correct answers were seen here. A number of candidates did not give a response.
notes.10ai: Most candidates answered this question well.
notes.10aii: Although some candidates answered correctly, a number of candidates did not give a response.
notes.10aiii: Candidates generally displayed good knowledge of the difference between planets near and far from the Sun.
notes.10aiv: Every candidate answered this question with most gaining full credit.
notes.10b: Many correct answers were seen here, generally with full working shown. Other answers usually gained credit for recall of the speed = distance / time equation which was usually rearranged correctly with correct values substituted.
